clauses.text:
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me by section 7 of the 
act of March 14, 1936, entitled “An act 
to provide for vacations to Government 
employees and for other purposes” (49 
Stat. 1161), it is ordered that section 15 
of Executive Order No. 7845, dated March 
21, 1938,1  prescribing regulations relat­
ing to annual leave of Government em­
ployees, be, and it is hereby, amended to 
read as follows:
“Sec. 15. Temporary employees who 
subsequently receive indefinite, emer­
gency, probational, or permanent ap­
pointments in the same department or 
agency without break in service shall be 
entitled to 2% days annual leave for 
each full month of service to the date of 
such indefinite, emergency, probational, 
or permanent appointment and thereaf­
ter at the rate of 2 y6  days per month, 
and shall be credited with such accumu­
lated and current accrued leave as may 
be due, or charged with any unaccrued 
leave which may have been advanced.”
This order shall be effective as of June 
30, 1939, and shall be published in the 
F ederal R egister.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 8226 original (4 FR 3722): one paragraph amending section 15 of EO 7845 (annual leave of Government employees), effective as of June 30, 1939; the held page also carries neighbouring EO 8225 and EO 8227, which I did not treat as part of this order. I read the held EO 8384 text (5 FR 1253, annual-leave regulations), and the same section also appears in the held 5 FR 1256 file (EO_8385.txt), which is the page-overlap source of ACT:EO:8226>EO:8385. Its Sec. 21 states 'This order shall supersede Executive Orders No. 7845 of March 21, 1938, No. 7879 of May 9, 1938, and No. 8226 of August 24, 1939' effective as of March 2, 1940. EO 8226 named by number and date is therefore expressly superseded in whole; it was only an amendment of a section of EO 7845, which is itself superseded by the same sentence, so no residual operative content remains. EO 8384 contains no savings clause for EO 8226; Sec. 20 ratifies temporary departmental regulations under EO 7321 and revokes inconsistent regulations, which concerns other instruments. The catalog note 'Revoked by: EO 8384' is consistent but only a lead. The older machine event from EO 7845 (amended by this order) is unrelated to ending. I found no earlier ending in the held record. Lifecycle details (exact effective-date chronology, any earlier statutory change) remain gaps; this is only a provisional NO hypothesis for owner consideration.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 8226 (August 24, 1939, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full in the held Federal Register text, amends section 15 of EO 7845 of March 21, 1938 (annual leave regulations) to read as follows (a rule that temporary employees who "subsequently receive indefinite," emergency, probational or permanent appointments without a break in service are entitled to stated annual leave), and the order is effective as of June 30, 1939. EO 8384 (March 29, 1940; 5 FR 1253, issue of Tuesday, April 2, 1940) prescribes new annual leave regulations and, in its section 21, states "This order shall supersede" EO 7845, EO 7879 and EO 8226 and the order is "effective as of March 2, 1940", except as to its own sections 6 and 9. EO 8226 has no term of its own, so the first end is that express supersession.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end is held. EO 8226 states no term or condition other than its own effective date. Searches of the held corpus for the number in the form Executive Order No. 8226 found EO 8384 (the supersession) and no other order that revokes or supersedes it. The effective-as-of wording in EO 8384 section 21 reaches back before the signing date (March 29, 1940) to March 2, 1940, and the claim records March 2, 1940 as the effective date of the supersession as the order's own words state; March 29, 1940 is the alternative reading for a reviewer who treats the retroactive date as not governing.","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives. The authority recital (section 7 of the act of March 14, 1936) is not a command and the order directs nothing apart from the restated section.","savings_check":"The substance of EO 8226 continues in the superseding order: section 15 of EO 8384 carries the same rule that temporary employees who \"subsequently receive indefinite,\" emergency, probational or permanent appointments in the same department or agency without a break in service are entitled to annual leave for each full month and are credited with accrued leave. Leave earned under EO 8226 between June 30, 1939 and March 2, 1940 is an accrued effect; the held EO 8384 text provides for adjustment of leave on the basis of its regulations in section 21 and no held source shows any loss of leave earned under EO 8226.","scope_check":"The inventory has one row for the whole order, a single restated section 15. The only exception in EO 8384 section 21 concerns its own sections 6 and 9, effective as of July 1, 1936, which do not concern the temporary-employee leave rule restated by EO 8226. The order was not amended or extended before its supersession. The restated section is standing text; if the amending command is read as fully performed on signing, the whole-order end date would not change because the order's only row is that restated section."}

savings_residuals.reason: The substance of EO 8226 continues in the superseding order: section 15 of EO 8384 carries the same rule that temporary employees who "subsequently receive indefinite," emergency, probational or permanent appointments in the same department or agency without a break in service are entitled to annual leave for each full month and are credited with accrued leave. Leave earned under EO 8226 between June 30, 1939 and March 2, 1940 is an accrued effect; the held EO 8384 text provides for adjustment of leave on the basis of its regulations in section 21 and no held source shows any loss of leave earned under EO 8226.

This order shall supersede 
Executive Orders No. 7845 of March 21, 
1938, No. 7879 of May 9, 1938, and No. 
8226 of August 24, 1939,1  and shall be 
effective as of March 2, 1940, except that 
sections 6 and 9 shall be effective as of 
July 1, 1936, provided that the total 
amount of leave to the credit of any em­
ployee resulting from an adjustment of 
such leave on the basis of the regulations 
as herein amended shall not exceed the 
amount authorized to be accumulated by 
law.
